title: Prefill window alignment and KV-epoching to eliminate nondeterministic CUDA graph capture divergence
creator: Emily Chen
description:
Problem: We observe rare but repeatable nondeterministic failures during CUDA graph capture and replay when multiple decode streams have slightly different prefill window boundaries. The RNG state, KV cache epoch, and per-stream prefill alignment occasionally cause graph re-capture that diverges (different kernel scheduling), leading to output mismatch and, in one customer case, an incorrect streaming token order. Root cause hypothesis: race between concurrent stream prefill completion and graph capture windowing combined with stale KV pointers (epoch mismatch).

Goals:
- Ensure deterministic capture/replay across concurrent streams for identical logical prefixes.
- Avoid unnecessary re-capture cycles while preserving low latency for short-lived streams.
- Provide clear fallback that preserves correctness when a capture mismatch is detected.

Success metrics (measurable):
- Reproduce rate of the failure in internal fuzz harness goes from ~0.8% to <0.01% across 1M randomized prefill+decode jobs.
- No >1% p95 latency regression for typical 8-token decode workloads.
- Zero production customer-impacted errors attributable to capture divergence across the next 30 days after rollout.

Design summary:
1) Prefill window alignment: introduce a lightweight prefill epoch alignment step at stream start. Each incoming request computes a prefill-window-hash (based on model-id, pinned-sequence-length-bucket, and prefix-length-modulo config) and is only batched into a capture window if its hash matches the in-progress capture slot. Streams with mismatched hashes are queued to the next window boundary rather than forcing an immediate cross-aligned capture. This reduces capture-time variance without increasing median latency for typical workloads.

2) KV-epoching: attach an explicit 64-bit epoch id to KV caches. The runtime increments the epoch when a mutation occurs that would invalidate earlier captures (e.g., quantized kernel selection, fused-attention fallback, or any prefill that changed buffer layout). Capture metadata includes the expected KV-epoch; replay validates it and triggers safe fallback if mismatched.

3) Deterministic seeding & capture fingerprinting: capture fingerprint includes kernel-config digest, prefill-window-hash, KV-epoch, and RNG-substate id. Replay performs exact match. If fingerprint mismatch is detected during replay, the runtime falls back to: (a) abort replay and execute eager decode on the current stream, and (b) schedule a deterministic recapture under exclusive capture mode to ensure the correct captured graph exists for subsequent replays.

4) Lightweight exclusive recapture mode: for recapture, we perform an exclusive small critical-section capture (bounded to 1ms on a warm GPU) to recapture a graph that matches the current fingerprint. The exclusive section serializes competing recaptures to avoid thrashing.

Implementation plan and milestones: 
- Spike (2 days): microbench harness to reproduce divergence deterministically (fuzzing different prefix lengths, concurrent stream counts, kernel fallback toggles). Owner: Raj.
- KV-epoch infra (3 days): plumbing epoch into KV cache structures, persist in capture metadata, API to bump epoch. Owner: Miguel Alvarez.
- Prefill-window hashing (2 days): implement hashing function + bucket config; ensure it is cheap and stable across process restarts. Owner: Priya Menon.
- Fingerprint & fallback logic (3 days): implement match logic and eager-fallback path with telemetry. Owner: Raj.
- Exclusive recapture (2 days): implement critical-section capture with metrics and backoff. Owner: Daniel Kim.
- QA harness + perf runs (4 days): run 1M-job fuzz suite, profile latency impact; tune bucket config. Owner: Sarah Johnson.
- Canary (1 week): staged rollout to internal accounts -> select hosted customers -> global. Rollout blockers defined. Owner: Emily.

Testing and verification:
- Unit tests: KV-epoch increments and edge cases (persist, overflow).
- Integration: deterministic reproduce test added to nightly fuzz harness; assert fingerprint invariant.
- Load/perf: regression runs on p95/p99 decode latency across 100k requests for small/medium prefixes.
- Chaos test: kill GPU process mid-capture and ensure fallback preserves correctness and metrics are emitted.

Observability & alerts:
- Emit metric runtime.capture.fingerprint_mismatch{reason} with tags: kernel_fallback, kv_epoch_mismatch, prefill_hash_mismatch.
- Alert: paging if mismatch rate > 0.1% over 5m for production clusters.
- Dashboard: graph capture miss rate, exclusive_recapture_count, eager_fallback_rate.

Rollout and mitigations:
- Feature flag: runtime.prefill_alignment_v2 (off by default).
- Step 1: internal canary (10% internal traffic) for 48h, check fuzz harness and metrics.
- Step 2: pilot with two low-latency customers, monitor.
- Step 3: gradual ramp if metrics stable.
- Emergency rollback: flip off feature flag to return to current capture behavior (rely on previous fallback).

Risks and trade-offs:
- Increased scheduling latency for a small fraction of tiny requests due to bucketing; mitigated by tuning bucket sizes.
- Additional complexity in capture metadata increases storage/compatibility concerns for long-lived graphs across upgrades; mitigated by versioning fingerprint schema.

Deliverables:
- Code changes in runtime/core and runtime/graph-capture modules (PRs linked in comments).
- New unit/integration tests in ci/fuzz and ci/integration.
- Dashboard and alert runbook.

Acceptance criteria:
- Fuzz harness metric <0.01% divergence after fixes.
- Canary latency regression <1% p95.
- No customer-impacting incidents during 7-day pilot.

2025-02-13 Raj Patel: Spike harness implemented; can reproduce divergence locally by orchestrating 3 concurrent streams with offsets [7, 8, 9] tokens and forcing kernel fallback. Reproducer in repo: github.com/redwood/runtime/compare/ENG-48123-spike (WIP).
2025-02-14 Miguel Alvarez: KV-epoch proto added to runtime KVCache class. Pushed branch: github.com/redwood/runtime/kv-epoch-proto (PR forthcoming). Early unit tests for epoch bump pass.

2025-02-16 Priya Menon: Prefill hashing algorithm PR ready for review. Using (model_id, seq_len_bucket, prefix_len % 4) -> xxhash64. Default buckets: [<=32, 33-128, >128]. Need review for bucket choices and effect on latency.
2025-02-17 Daniel Kim: Implemented exclusive recapture lock with exponential backoff; added telemetry metric exclusive_recapture_count. Microbench shows 0.3ms median extra on recapture path.

2025-02-18 Sarah Johnson: Started large-scale fuzz run (200k jobs so far). Observed mismatch rate drop from 0.8% -> 0.06% with default bucket config. Next: iterate on bucket sizing to reduce to target <0.01%.

2025-02-19 Raj Patel: Added eager fallback path and deterministic fingerprint check in replay. Open PR: github.com/redwood/runtime/pull/4532. Requesting design review from Emily and Miguel before merging to main.

2025-02-20 Emily Chen: Reviewed and approved KV-epoch approach; asked to add schema versioning to fingerprint to support graceful upgrades. Also requested runbook for turning off runtime.prefill_alignment_v2 in Hosted.
